Sony Culture Entertainment Inc. (SCU), was a Japanese entertainment company wholly owned subsidiary by Sony Group Corporation. It was initial a split off from the original Sony Music Entertainment Inc on April 1, 2003. Because the original Sony Music Entertainment decided that reorganize all non-music businesses into this new company. Later on, the company split and sold its retail and cosmetics business to a third parties. It eventually remerged with second generation of Sony Music Entertainment Inc. , making the current Sony Music Entertainment (Japan) on Decemeber 1, 2006.
Company Profile
*Company Name: Sony Culture Entertainment Inc.
*Headquarters: 4–5 Rokubanchō
*Original Company Established: April 1, 2003
*Bussiness Area: Shareholding and management of subsidiaries
*Representative: Representative Director and CEO, Tsutomu Hata (as of May 1, 2005)
*Capital: 100 million yen
*Shareholder: Sony Corporation (later Sony Group Corporation)
They used to have SME Shirokanedai building when they split, but before remerge they sold that building.
Company History
*April 1, 2003 - The company's predecessor, Sony Music Entertainment (Japan), wanted split to form Sony Culture Entertainment Inc., which included all non-music businesses SMEJ originally have.
*May 17, 2006 - In accordance with Sony Corporation's policy of operating its retail business independently, Sony Culture Entertainment Inc. was renamed SCU Corporation and split again. The retail business was spun off into Styling Life Holdings Inc., and the remaining non-retail businesses were established as a new Sony Culture Entertainment Inc. At the same time, it was announced that SCU Corporation would merge with its parent company, Sony Corporation.
*December 1, 2006 - It remerged with Sony Music Entertainment (Japan), and Sony Culture Entertainment Inc. was dissolved.
Group Companies
Non Retail bussiness
*Sony Creative Product
*Sony Magazine
*Aniplex
*DreamLaunch Inc.
*ClipGate Inc.
*Music_On!_TV
*Zepp
Retail bussiness
Spun off itself as StylingLife Group and sold:
*LightUp Shopping Club (formerly Sony Family Club, renamed May 1, 2006)
*B&C Labs (formerly Sony CP Labs, renamed January 1, 2006)
*CP Cosmetics (spun off from B&C Labs on January 4, 2006)
*LifeNeo
The following companies were not sold as above during the separation, but have also left the Sony Group:
*Maxim's Paris Japan (ceased operations in 2015, liquidated by mid-2015)
*PlazaStyle (formerly Sony Plaza, renamed May 1, 2006, later acquired by StylingLife Group on May 5, 2010)
